market_name: Will 3 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market probability move persists or fades; cross-check 2y and 10y Treasury yields and fed funds futures (SOFR/ZQ) for confirmation.
time_plan.1h: Confirm TLT price reaction vs. move in 2y yield; look for any Fed speaker headlines or data prints (CPI, jobs) that could explain the shift.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether the yield move is broad-based (curve shift) or idiosyncratic; check dollar index for corroboration.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether move was already public (scheduled data/FOMC minutes) vs. genuine leak; scale conviction accordingly.
time_plan.12h: Mark TLT return vs. entry; note whether directional thesis held and whether magnitude stayed well below the 700bp tradable bar.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of three 25bp Fed cuts in 2026 is a dovish signal implying a lower expected policy-rate path. Lower expected front-end and terminal rates pull the whole curve down, and duration-heavy TLT rallies as yields fall. Conversely a drop in the probability would push TLT down. Directional read assumes the anomaly is a dovish shift.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and real-yield (TIP) direction to confirm the dovish read; verify gold spot/GLD reaction.
time_plan.1h: Compare gold move to Treasury move for internal consistency of the easing thesis.
time_plan.2h: Watch for competing drivers (geopolitical risk bid, equity risk-on/off) that could dominate gold independent of rates.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether the catalyst was public data; downgrade if move mean-reverts.
time_plan.12h: Record GLD return; confirm the move stayed far under 700bp and note thesis accuracy.

predictions.reasoning: A dovish shift toward more 2026 cuts lowers real yields and typically weakens the dollar, both supportive of gold. Gold is a liquid, broadly-traded proxy for Fed-easing expectations. The effect is second-order and noisy, so confidence is modest and direction flips if the probability move is hawkish.

evidence_used: Market question ties resolution to number of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a direct rate-expectations gauge
Standard macro transmission: dovish rate path -> lower yields, weaker USD, higher gold and long bonds
TLT and GLD are highly liquid ETF proxies for these channels
uncertainty_notes: Direction depends entirely on which way the implied probability moved; the prompt gives no move direction, so the mapping assumes a dovish shift
12h asset moves from a single prediction-market shift are typically tens of bps, far below the 700bp tradable threshold — not tradable
Fed-cut probabilities usually move on public data (CPI, payrolls, FOMC), so leakage/edge is unlikely
'military_conflict' topic tag appears mislabeled; treated as a pure monetary-policy market

llm_justification.summary: This is a US monetary-policy market on the count of 2026 Fed rate cuts, a clean rate-expectations sensor. A sharp rise in the probability of three cuts is a dovish signal implying a lower policy-rate path, which would lift long Treasuries (TLT) and gold (GLD) while pressuring the dollar; a hawkish drop would reverse these. Realistic 12h magnitudes are tens of bps, well under the 700bp tradable bar, so this is research-only with modest confidence.
key_assumptions: The observed anomaly is a meaningfully sized dovish shift in cut probability
Standard rate-transmission channels dominate over idiosyncratic flows in the 12h window
The move is not already fully reflected via a public data release
failure_modes: Probability actually moved hawkish, flipping both directions
Move driven by public FOMC/data event already priced into TLT and GLD
Risk-on equity rally or geopolitical bid overrides the rate channel for gold
Small, noisy prediction-market move with no genuine informational edge
Curve reshaping (front-end vs long-end) means TLT reacts opposite to a front-loaded-cut narrative
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
